tools_used: metrics/statpack.md (CVSG cut, relist cut, sal-v4 band table)
web fetch (supremecourt.gov docket page and PDFs, SCOTUSblog, certpool)
subagent digest of provisioned petition and BIO text
helpful: The sal-v4 band table matching context.salience_version gave an unambiguous pooled anchor for a `high` band CVSG cell.
Provisioned petition and BIO text allowed the vehicle read (Gospel Light not a petitioner, PI posture, pending state appeal) without any fetching, and the SG brief later confirmed those points.
Forward-mode permission to read this docket's own post-baseline entries was the whole forecast here: the SG's hold recommendation is not inferable from an eleven-month-old snapshot.
gaps: No PDF text extraction on the runner: WebFetch returns raw PDF bytes for supremecourt.gov filings and the Read tool needs poppler. I had to `uv run --with pypdf` to read the SG brief. A provisioned `sg-brief.txt` for CVSG cells whose SG brief has been filed, or a PDF-to-text helper, would remove this.
The CourtListener MCP carries no docket entries for SCOTUS dockets, so the sanctioned live path cannot answer 'what has happened on this docket since the snapshot' for a forward cell.
The statpack has no cut for CVSG petitions by SG recommendation (grant / deny / hold) or for held petitions' eventual disposition; both P(hold) and P(GVR | lead case reverses) had to be judgment.
`fedcourts query` has no filter for CVSG status or relist count, so it could not return comparable priors for this cell; its default ranking put interim applications first.
notes: About 16 retrieval calls, under budget. The snapshot for a `moment: cvsg` cell is fixed at the CVSG date by design, so on a run eleven months later the provisioned baseline and the live docket diverge sharply; the reasoning states which is which.
